course.title: Generative AI — From Beginner to Professional
course.description: A visual-first, project-based generative AI curriculum preserving the supplied 227-topic syllabus across foundations, model architectures, prompt/API development, RAG, agents, multimodal systems, evaluation, security, governance, production, and optional specialist research.
course.version_scope: Documentation snapshot reviewed 2026-10-17. Examples use Python 3.11+ syntax and provider-neutral design where practical; selected OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, PyTorch, Microsoft, OWASP, NIST, and MCP references are linked as examples of primary documentation. Provider/model identifiers, pricing, quotas, policies, SDKs, and regulations change and must be checked for a specific implementation.
prerequisites: Basic computer skills are sufficient to start.
Python, elementary mathematics, and API familiarity become increasingly useful in later modules.
Advanced mathematics is revisited as needed and is not a requirement before trying pretrained models.
course.estimated_learning_time: Approximately 4–8 months of consistent part-time study, depending on programming experience, project depth, and optional specializations.
learning_outcomes: Explain generative AI and distinguish it from traditional AI and predictive/discriminative systems.
Understand neural networks, transformers, LLMs, embeddings, diffusion models, and other generative approaches.
Design and evaluate prompts, integrate model APIs, and validate structured outputs.
Build a document question-answering/RAG prototype and a bounded tool-using workflow.
Work with text, images, audio, video, code, and synthetic data while assessing modality-specific limitations.
Evaluate model quality, hallucinations, retrieval, reliability, privacy, safety, cost, and latency.
Choose between prompting, retrieval, fine-tuning, hosted inference, and local model options using measurable trade-offs.
Document a production-oriented design with testing, security controls, monitoring, governance, and acknowledged limitations.
